children.text: Seasonal and Annual Mean Maritime Surface Weather and Sea Data, and Seasonal Upper-level Winds and Temperature for the USSR (pub.1950)
Publication Title: Morskoi Atlas = Marine atlas. Text in Russian.   For full detailed English translation see 'An Evaluation of the "Morskoi Atlas" (With Translations from Volumes I and II)'.
The Morskoi Atlas is devided into three parts: Volume I, navigation and geography; Volume II, physical geography; Volume III, military and political geography.

Contains a comprehensive treatment of the marine environment of the earth.  Contains sea charts and maps of important ports and naval bases, bathymetry, sea level, nature and velocity of currents, ice boundaries, ocean routes, national frontiers, earthquakes, volcanos, sediments, sea surface temperature, salinity, and density, range of tides, wind waves and swell, distribution of cetacea, sirenia, pinnipeds, ocean fishes, marine birds and algae, atmospheric pressure, cloudiness, fog, and storms.

A basic cartographic manual of ocean and seas.  This publication is in the National Climatic Data Center's Foreign Data Library, and is one of many books, atlases, maps, charts and other printed materials received by the NCDC from many nations over the years.

independently_reopened_public_reference_.short_quote: U.S.S.R. VOENNO-MORSKOE MINISTERSTVO. Morskoi Atlas (Marine Atlas). Moscow: 1950-1958. 3 v. LC 56-45955.
independently_reopened_public_reference_.independent_assessment: Parsed entry puts the institution in the responsibility position defined by the bibliography introduction. The entry identifies the whole three-volume set, matching the specific publication name and three-part scope in FGDC-2552. It does not identify an individual editor for every volume or establish XML authorship.

independently_reopened_public_reference_.locator: Header PDF0 and atlas row PDF88
independently_reopened_public_reference_.short_quote: Main Author; Morskoĭ atlas / Soviet Union. Voenno-morskoe ministerstvo.
independently_reopened_public_reference_.independent_assessment: The library catalogue independently places the historical corporate name in its main-author column. It corroborates the atlas holding, while the AAG entry supplies the explicit complete-set match. Neither an original atlas title page nor a modern institutional identity was inspected/inferred.

independently_reopened_public_reference_.short_quote: Japan Meteorological Agency; Average water temperature data developed by the Meteorological Agency; ADJSUBS(JMA); PACSUBS(JMA)
independently_reopened_public_reference_.independent_assessment: The report separates observation collection and format conversion from institutional development of average temperature products. The adjacent product table identifies the two monthly series and their100/200/400m depths. Read together, this supports JMA development credit for the exact analyzed products, not credit for all input observations or a conclusion derived merely from database operation. The table archive dates precede the2005 XML metadata.

independently_reopened_public_reference_.short_quote: Monthly Mean Subsurface Temperatures in seas around Japan
independently_reopened_public_reference_.independent_assessment: Monthly series at three depths and the121E/24N to161E/48N domain match FGDC-3954. Method changes and references are distinct from the product; no method-paper author becomes a creator.

Monthly series at three depths and the80W/20S to120E/60N domain match FGDC-3956. The broader Pacific product is distinct from the Japan-region product; no later replacement product or method author is substituted.

role_and_identity_limits: The selected credits are bibliography/institutional product credits supported by linked external evidence; they are not original FGDC origin text, XML authorship, copyright ownership or institutional operation alone.

The USSR literal origin remains present in the source and preservation notes. The two Japan primary origins remain exact text=null empty elements. Name-only creator objects add no type, affiliation, identifier, modern organization identity or person role.

The atlas abstract itself identifies the three-volume publication; the review does not select a particular volume, convert source1950 to the external1950-1958 span or use translation editors as creators.

Both temperature products match original frequency/depth/domain and historical series labels. Input-observation suppliers, distribution contacts and method-paper authors are not promoted into creator fields.

All prior412 cohorts/members/source contexts, notes and external-evidence requirements must remain unchanged. No other19 creator hold or any resource/date/title/alias/identity/DOI condition is cleared.

external_evidence_boundary.evidence_form: Parsed web text and exact hash-bound local reviewer excerpts, not retained original remote PDF/HTML bytes.
external_evidence_boundary.pdf_screenshot_attempts: Four requested bibliography/JODC pages failed because web screenshot was unavailable; no visual inspection claim is made.

fresh_measurement_requirements: Bind a fresh current before and actual after for each source. Supplied projected after hashes are historical projection evidence, not promised runtime hashes.

Existing creator preparation changes the embedded Curator decision creator stanza and appends required preservation notes with its established separators. Account for precisely those note changes plus creator objects; require all other full metadata fields unchanged and preserve all source XML.
